Delivered: `assessment.json`, `assessment.md` (1040 words), and `proposed-addendum/assemble-records.d9-obligation.patch` under my directory only. Nothing in source, tools or drafts was touched.

## Answer to the bounded question

**The obligation legitimately belongs later.** What is owed is a *successor artifact published by the D9 exit-contract unit* — a new normative source artifact. Publishing it in this application would mint reviewed-normative bytes independent20 never saw, forcing a new freeze and new design review of an artifact its owning unit hasn't authored. The existing normative rules already assign phase and owner: `owedBy` "the D9 exit-contract unit"; `neverDischargedByRepinning` "Publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit"; `whatIsNotOwed` "Nothing in the product source."

## Source claims all hold against actual selectors

I verified the manifest SHA by recomputation, then checked every assertion rather than trusting it. Inherited enum: 11 members, no `host-invariant`. `SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE` already in the inherited closed `errorCodes` with no preimage — so the "total and injective" precision note is right and the earlier non-totality claim was indeed wrong. Selected `D9FaultCause`: exactly the inherited set ∪ `{host-invariant}` = 12. Inherited artifact byte-exact, and the draft application already pins that same digest. `check-integration.py` really does hold all three halves.

**No admitted current consumer is forced to the inherited 11.** `workflows-and-surfaces.md` §0 supersedes the field closure with `StepTermination` (→12 via `$ref`), §9 enumerates all eleven non-`none` causes including `host-invariant`, and §2764 of `native-evidence.md` routes it. Only a reader validating against v1.14 alone gets 11 — the disclosed residue the obligation exists for.

## Finding D9-APP-1 (SHOULD, application-only)

The application would **not** falsely discharge the obligation — DR-007 stays HARD-BLOCKED naming "D9 successor to v1.14", condition 5 stays NOT MET, and the assembler literally writes "CARRIED-UNCHANGED does not grade or discharge an inherited residual."

But the obligation is **invisible**: `host-invariant` occurs zero times across `application-assembly.v1` and all 17 draft afterimages; `current-source-map.proposed.md` has no row for `d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json` despite every inherited chapter being told to read through that map and its middle column being "Potentially misleading selector"; DR-011-R08's text mentions only "old v1.14 ordering/goldens remain the inherited baseline". Meanwhile condition 1 is asserted MET via those very dispositions. True but unfindable — an omission, not a false claim.

## Remedy

A `carriedCrossUnitObligation` field on exactly two rows of `inherited-residuals.applied.v1.json`, pinned by JSON-pointer `ref()` into the frozen snapshot, with three `assert`s guarding minting on the accepted bytes still carrying it, and an explicit `notDischargedBy` naming condition 1, ACCEPT-DESIGN, activation and the final application review. Owner, artifact, member, target code and selectors are all named — not a vague future gate.

**No new source freeze or design review needed** for this. I deliberately rejected adding the map row: that file is inside the frozen subject, and the product contract already routes consumers correctly, so it would buy little at the cost of a re-freeze.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The interesting structural point is *where an obligation has to live to survive*. The source put it in the native route registry with a self-aware note that "a later pass reading this registry alone cannot mistake it for closed" — but later passes read the **applied records**, not the route registry. An obligation's durability is a property of its position in the actual reading path, not of how emphatically it is worded.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Limitations, stated plainly: bounded read (not the other contracts, six checks, or 32 gates); `check-integration.py` was read, not executed; the patch is unapplied and untested since no accepted inputs exist to run a real assembly. This is one assessor's account — Codex agreement, independent20, NEWblind9 and root review all still stand.
